gen.title: Core ideas about variation and data summarization

cards.stem: What is the stated use for descriptive statistics when working with population data?
options: summarize a collection of population data
create new allele variants in a lab
measure physical isolation between groups
cards.quote: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize a collection of population data in a clear and concise manner.
cards.hint: Think about summarizing large sets clearly and concisely

cards.stem: In biology, how is a population described in terms of breeding behavior?
options: breed primarily or solely among themselves
share identical allele frequencies always
maintain uniform racial boundaries
cards.quote: In biology, a population generally denotes a group whose members breed primarily or solely among themselves.
cards.hint: Consider who members primarily breed with

cards.stem: Which belief about human groups is called a common misconception on the page?
options: uniform groups with large biological differences
ethnicity always matches familial origins
allele frequencies never change over time
cards.quote: A common misconception is that human populations fall into uniform groups with large biological differences, which lie along racial boundaries.
cards.hint: Focus on ideas about uniformity and racial boundaries

cards.stem: What does research conclude about racial classifications and genetic variation?
options: inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation
precise estimators of allele frequencies
determined solely by physical isolation
cards.quote: Research has demonstrated that racial classifications are inadequate descriptors of the distribution of genetic variation in the human species.
cards.hint: Recall the finding about inadequacy for describing variation
